records.gloss: For the director. A psalm of David.
pieces: For the music director. A psalm of David.

L.1: For the director. A psalm of David.

R.1: For the leader of the music. A song of David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: the last group of David's psalms
decisions.reason: Psalms 138-145 are the last group of psalms headed "of David". Psalms 140-143 are all prayers for rescue from enemies who lay traps, plot and slander.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

records.heading: Rescue me from violent people

records.source: חַלְּצֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה מֵאָדָ֣ם רָ֑ע מֵאִ֖ישׁ חֲמָסִ֣ים תִּנְצְרֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Rescue me, YHWH, from humankind evil; from [the] man of violences preserve me,
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, rescue me from evil people; keep me safe from those who do violence,

L.2: Rescue me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, from evil humankind; from {{gender:the person|the man}} of violence preserve me,

R.2: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save me from evil people. Protect me from people who hurt others.

decisions.choice: the man of violence: a kind of person, many people
decisions.reason: Both phrases are singular in the Hebrew ("evil humankind", "the man of violences"), but verse 3 goes on with "they": the singular stands for everyone of that kind.

decisions.choice: violence: harm done to others, lawless cruelty
decisions.reason: The word (chamas) is violence and injustice done to people, the sin that filled the earth before the flood (Genesis 6:11). The plural here makes it stronger: a person made of violence.

decisions.choice: evil people; those who do violence
alternatives: the evil man; the violent man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the singular stands for (m1), a whole group, which includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the singular with a gender setting.

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֤ר חָשְׁב֣וּ רָע֣וֹת בְּלֵ֑ב כָּל־י֝֗וֹם יָג֥וּרוּ מִלְחָמֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: who plan evil things in [the] heart; every day they stir up wars.
pieces: who scheme harm in their hearts and keep starting battles day after day.

L.3: who plan evil things in [the] heart; every day they stir up wars.

R.3: They make evil plans in their minds. Every day they start fights.

decisions.choice: stir up: provoke, start
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) can mean to stir up strife, or to gather as a band and attack (56:7; 59:4). Either way the enemies are always looking for a fight.

decisions.choice: in the heart: in the mind, in secret
decisions.reason: The heart is where people think and plan. Their evil is plotted before it is done.

decisions.choice: in their minds
decisions.reason: Readable says where the planning happens in plain words (m2).

records.source: שָֽׁנֲנ֣וּ לְשׁוֹנָם֮ כְּֽמוֹ־נָ֫חָ֥שׁ חֲמַ֥ת עַכְשׁ֑וּב תַּ֖חַת שְׂפָתֵ֣ימוֹ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: They sharpen their tongue like a snake; venom of a viper [is] under their lips. Selah.
pieces: They whet their tongues like a serpent; viper's venom lies hidden behind their lips. Selah

L.4: They sharpen their tongue like a snake; [the] venom of a viper [is] under their lips. Selah

R.4: Their words are as dangerous as a snake's bite. What they say is like deadly poison. Selah

decisions.choice: quoted in Romans 3:13
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the second line, from the ancient Greek translation ("the poison of asps is under their lips"), with 5:10 and other psalms, to show that all people are under sin (Romans 3:9-18).

decisions.choice: viper: a poisonous snake
decisions.reason: The word ('akhshuv) is found only here. The ancient Greek translation has "asp"; it is some poisonous creature, most likely a snake.

decisions.choice: sharpen their tongue: make their words wound
decisions.reason: Words are pictured as weapons that cut and poison (52:4; 64:4). A snake's tongue was thought of as the source of its venom.

decisions.choice: their words are as dangerous as a snake's bite
alternatives: they sharpen their tongues like a snake
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m3): the danger is in what they say.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.source: שָׁמְרֵ֤נִי יְהוָ֨ה׀מִ֘ידֵ֤י רָשָׁ֗ע מֵאִ֣ישׁ חֲמָסִ֣ים תִּנְצְרֵ֑נִי אֲשֶׁ֥ר חָ֝שְׁב֗וּ לִדְח֥וֹת פְּעָמָֽי׃
records.gloss: Keep me, YHWH, from [the] hands of [the] wicked; from [the] man of violences preserve me, who have planned to push down my steps.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, guard me from the clutches of the wicked; shield me from violent people who are scheming to make me fall.

L.5: Keep me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, from [the] hands of [the] wicked; from {{gender:the person|the man}} of violence preserve me, [those] who have planned to trip up my steps.

R.5: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, keep me out of the hands of evil people. Protect me from violent people. They are planning to make me fall.

decisions.choice: the hands of the wicked: their power
decisions.reason: To be in someone's hands is to be in their power.

decisions.choice: the man of violence ... who have planned
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the singular stands for a group: the verb after it is plural.

decisions.choice: push down my steps: make me stumble and fall
decisions.reason: The picture is of walking on a path and being tripped, as the traps of verse 6 go on to show.

decisions.choice: violent people
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: טָֽמְנֽוּ־גֵאִ֨ים׀פַּ֡ח לִ֗י וַחֲבָלִ֗ים פָּ֣רְשׂוּ רֶ֭שֶׁת לְיַד־מַעְגָּ֑ל מֹקְשִׁ֖ים שָֽׁתוּ־לִ֣י סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: They have hidden, [the] proud, a trap for me and cords; they have spread a net at [the] side of [the] track; snares they have set for me. Selah.
pieces: Arrogant people have hidden a trap for me; they have stretched out ropes as a net beside the path and laid snares to catch me. Selah

L.6: [The] proud have hidden a trap for me, and cords; they have spread a net by [the] side of [the] path; snares they have set for me. Selah

R.6: Proud people have hidden a trap to catch me. They have spread out a net of ropes beside the road. They have set traps for me. Selah

decisions.choice: trap, net, snares: the hunter's tools
decisions.reason: Birds and animals were caught with hidden traps, nets of cord and snares (91:3; 124:7). The enemies hunt the psalmist like prey, setting traps along the path he walks (142:4).

decisions.choice: cords ... a net: they spread cords as a net
alternatives: a trap and cords they have hidden; they have spread a net
decisions.reason: "Cords" can belong with the trap that was hidden, or with the net that was spread (a net made of cords). The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the proud: the arrogant, who do not fear God
decisions.reason: The proud (ge'im) are those who think they need answer to no one (94:2).

records.source: אָמַ֣רְתִּי לַ֭יהוָה אֵ֣לִי אָ֑תָּה הַאֲזִ֥ינָה יְ֝הוָ֗ה ק֣וֹל תַּחֲנוּנָֽי׃
records.gloss: I have said to YHWH, My God [are] you; give ear, YHWH, [to the] voice of my supplications.
pieces: I have told {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "You are my God." Turn {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to the sound of my pleading.

L.7: I have said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "My God [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}." Give ear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, to the voice of my pleas for mercy.

R.7: I said to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "You are my God." {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please listen when I beg {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for help.

decisions.choice: supplications: pleas for mercy
decisions.reason: The word (tachanunim) comes from the verb "to show favor": it is a plea to be treated with mercy (28:2; 130:2).

decisions.choice: give ear: listen closely
decisions.reason: To give ear is to turn and listen (5:2; 17:1).

decisions.choice: My God are you: a confession of trust
decisions.reason: The psalmist claims the LORD as his own God, as in 31:15. His plea rests on that bond.

records.source: יְהֹוִ֣ה אֲ֭דֹנָי עֹ֣ז יְשׁוּעָתִ֑י סַכֹּ֥תָה לְ֝רֹאשִׁ֗י בְּי֣וֹם נָֽשֶׁק׃
records.gloss: YHWH [the] Lord, strength of my salvation, you have covered my head in [the] day of weapons.
pieces: Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, mighty one who saves me, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have covered my head on the day the weapons clash.

L.8: {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} my Lord, strength of my salvation, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have covered my head in [the] day of weapons.

R.8: Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are strong and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} save me. You protected my head like a helmet when I was in battle.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord: the divine name and the title
decisions.reason: Here the name comes before the title "my Lord" ('Adonai), as in 68:21 and 109:21. The name is then read aloud as "God" so as not to say "Lord" twice.

decisions.choice: strength of my salvation: the strong one who saves me
decisions.reason: The phrase names God as the power behind the psalmist's rescue (28:8).

decisions.choice: covered my head: protected me in battle
decisions.reason: God has been like a helmet to him (60:9 calls Ephraim "the helmet of my head"). "The day of weapons" is a day of battle.

decisions.choice: GOD my Lord (L); Lord GOD (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 68:21: the name is written GOD so that the two are not read as "Lord Lord"; Balanced and Readable use the familiar order, with "Lord" in address.

decisions.choice: protected my head like a helmet
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the picture (m3).

records.source: אַל־תִּתֵּ֣ן יְ֭הוָה מַאֲוַיֵּ֣י רָשָׁ֑ע זְמָמ֥וֹ אַל־תָּ֝פֵ֗ק יָר֥וּמוּ סֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: Do not grant, YHWH, [the] desires of [the] wicked; his plan do not further; they would be exalted. Selah.
pieces: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not give the wicked what they crave; do not let their scheme succeed, or they will grow proud. Selah

L.9: Do not grant, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, the desires of the wicked; do not further his scheme, [or] they will be exalted. Selah

R.9: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, do not let evil people get what they want. Do not let their plans work, or they will become proud. Selah

decisions.choice: they will be exalted: they would grow proud
alternatives: they rise up (joined with verse 10: "those around me raise their head")
decisions.reason: The last word (yarumu) is short and hard to place. It can be the result of their success ("or they will be exalted"), or it can begin the next line, "they lift up the head, those who surround me".

decisions.choice: his plan: a wicked scheme
decisions.reason: The word (zemam) is a plan, here an evil plot, as the verb in 37:12.

decisions.choice: the wicked ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew describes "the wicked" as one person ("he", "his") who stands for all who act this way. Balanced and Readable make the portrait plural, which is how "the wicked" is heard in English and includes men and women alike; Literal keeps the Hebrew singular.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

records.gloss: [The] head of those surrounding me — [the] trouble of their lips, may it cover them.
pieces: As for those who close in around me, may the harm their own lips speak come down over their heads.

L.10: [As for the] head of those who surround me, may the trouble of their lips cover them.

R.10: My enemies are all around me. Let the evil they say about others fall back on them.

decisions.choice: may it cover them: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this word in one form and its notes say to read it in another. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: the trouble of their lips: the harm they speak
alternatives: their leader's head (the head as the chief)
decisions.reason: The harm they plan with words (verse 4) is to come down on their own heads, as in 7:17. "Head" may be the head of each enemy or the chief among them.

decisions.choice: My enemies are all around me.
alternatives: As for the head of those around me
decisions.reason: Readable makes a short sentence of the opening phrase and names who is meant.

records.source: יִמּ֥וֹטוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֗ם גֶּֽחָ֫לִ֥ים בָּאֵ֥שׁ יַפִּלֵ֑ם בְּ֝מַהֲמֹר֗וֹת בַּֽל־יָקֽוּמוּ׃
records.gloss: May they drop on them, burning coals; into the fire may he make them fall, into pits, [that] not they rise.
pieces: Let burning coals rain down on them; may they be hurled into fire, into deep pits, never to get up again.

L.11: May burning coals drop upon them; into the fire may [one] cast them, into deep pits, [so that] they do not rise.

R.11: May red-hot coals land on them. May they be pitched into fire, into deep holes they can never climb out of.

decisions.choice: may they drop: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this word in one form and its notes say to read it in another. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: burning coals and fire: judgment from heaven
decisions.reason: Coals and fire fall on the wicked in 11:6 and 18:13-14, recalling the fire that fell on Sodom (Genesis 19:24).

decisions.choice: pits: deep pits, perhaps watery ones
decisions.reason: The word (mahamorot) is found only here. It is some deep place from which no one comes up, like the pit of the dead.

decisions.choice: a prayer for judgment on the violent
decisions.reason: As in 5:11, the psalmist does not take revenge himself. He asks God to bring the harm these people plan back on them, and leaves the judgment to God.

decisions.choice: may they be hurled (B); may they be pitched (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "may he cast them" names no one; Balanced and Readable use the passive so that no subject is supplied, as Literal does with "[one]".

records.source: אִ֥ישׁ לָשׁוֹן֮ בַּל־יִכּ֪וֹן בָּ֫אָ֥רֶץ אִישׁ־חָמָ֥ס רָ֑ע יְ֝צוּדֶ֗נּוּ לְמַדְחֵפֹֽת׃
records.gloss: A man of tongue not let him be established in the land; a man of violence — evil let it hunt him to blows.
pieces: Let no slanderer find a firm place in the land; let disaster hunt down the violent and strike them again and again.

L.12: {{gender:A person|A man}} of tongue — let {{gender:them|him}} not be established in the land; {{gender:a person|a man}} of violence — let evil hunt {{gender:them|him}} down with blow upon blow.

R.12: Do not let people who tell lies about others last in the land. Let trouble chase violent people and knock them down.

decisions.choice: a man of tongue: a slanderer
decisions.reason: A "man of tongue" is one who does harm with what he says, the slanderer of 101:5.

decisions.choice: blows: thrust after thrust, until they fall
decisions.reason: The word (madchefot) is found only here; it comes from a verb "to push, drive". Evil is pictured as a hunter that drives them on until they fall.

decisions.choice: be established: last, stand firm
decisions.reason: The verb (kun) is used of what is set firm and lasts (89:38; 101:7).

decisions.choice: the slanderer ... the violent ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable speak of the kind of person meant, in the plural where needed; Literal keeps the singular with a gender setting.

records.source: יָדַ֗עְתִּי כִּֽי־יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה יְ֭הוָה דִּ֣ין עָנִ֑י מִ֝שְׁפַּ֗ט אֶבְיֹנִֽים׃
records.gloss: I know that YHWH will do [the] cause of [the] poor, [the] justice of [the] needy.
pieces: I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will take up the case of the oppressed and see that the needy get justice.

L.13: I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will uphold [the] cause of [the] poor, [and] justice for [the] needy.

R.13: I know that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will defend poor people and make sure that people in need are treated fairly.

decisions.choice: I know: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text writes this word in one form and its notes say to read it in another. The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: the cause of the poor: their case before a judge
decisions.reason: The word (din) is a legal case. The LORD acts as judge and as advocate for the poor ('ani), the afflicted who have no one else to speak for them (9:5; 10:18).

decisions.choice: the needy: the poor who must depend on others
decisions.reason: The word ('evyon) is often paired with "poor" (40:18; 109:22). The psalmist counts himself among them.

records.source: אַ֣ךְ צַ֭דִּיקִים יוֹד֣וּ לִשְׁמֶ֑ךָ יֵשְׁב֥וּ יְ֝שָׁרִ֗ים אֶת־פָּנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Surely [the] righteous will give thanks to your name; [the] upright will dwell with your face.
pieces: The righteous will surely give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, and people of integrity will make their home before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

L.14: Surely [the] righteous will give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name; [the] upright will dwell in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence.

R.14: People who do what is right will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. Honest people will live close to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: your name: God himself, as he has shown himself
decisions.reason: The name stands for God as he is known by what he has done (5:12; 54:8).

decisions.choice: dwell with your face: live in God's presence
decisions.reason: To live before God's face is to be near him and in his favor, as guests in his house (11:7; 15:1; 23:6).

decisions.choice: for who you are
decisions.reason: Readable says what the name stands for (m1).

decisions.choice: people who do what is right; honest people
decisions.reason: As in 1:5 (tsaddiq); the upright (yashar) are those who are straight and honest.
